a1_answer:
NOVELTY STATEMENT — Standard practice tracks partial discharge magnitude (pC) during offline tests. My observable is the rate of change of partial discharge inception voltage (PDIV) across multiple outages, which captures the progressive weakening of insulation integrity before significant discharge activity appears. PDIV is more sensitive to early-stage insulation degradation than discharge magnitude alone because it reflects the voltage at which ionization first occurs, which decreases as insulation microvoids and delamination develop.

PHYSICS CHECK — PDIV is governed by the Townsend avalanche criterion: V_pd = B·d·ln(A·d/p), where d is insulation thickness, p is pressure, and A,B are material constants. For typical motor insulation, PDIV decreases by 5-15% when insulation integrity is compromised but before discharge magnitude increases significantly. A 6-month prediction window corresponds to a PDIV degradation rate of 0.5-1.5% per outage, which is detectable with standard PD testing equipment.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — Components: 1) Standard offline PD test equipment (already available), 2) High-voltage coupling capacitor (existing), 3) PD measurement analyzer (existing), 4) Data logging software (standard off-the-shelf). Materials: Standard test leads and connectors. Procedure: During scheduled outages, perform PDIV test using the IEEE 1434 standard method. Measure PDIV at 1.2x rated voltage (4.992 kV) with 60-second intervals. Record PDIV value and compare with historical data from previous outages. No new hardware required; only standard test procedure modification.

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — Installability: Same (uses existing test equipment). Operability: Same (same test duration, same personnel requirements). Maintenance: Same (no additional maintenance). Cost class: Same (no additional equipment costs). The approach requires no continuous monitoring hardware and uses existing offline testing procedures, maintaining parity with standard practice while providing earlier detection.

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Perform PDIV tests during three consecutive scheduled outages at 6-month intervals. Instruments: Standard PD test system with 4.992 kV capability, data logger. Pass threshold: PDIV degradation rate <1.5% per outage over three measurements. Fail threshold: PDIV degradation rate >1.5% per outage or PDIV decrease >15% from baseline. Duration: Three outages (18 months total). Kill criterion: If PDIV degradation exceeds 1.5% per outage at any point, the predictor is falsified as it would indicate either imminent failure (<6 months) or that the PDIV rate is not correlated with ground fault timing.
